Access.doc:
What you let one agent reach on its computer, beyond your Calimero apps:
these folders, a shell, the web. Yours to set (`set_access`); the agent's
runtime enforces it before any tool runs, and an agent with none set keeps
its runtime's default.

AccessView.doc: What you let one agent reach, as settings shows it.

Action.doc:
One thing your agent did, or wants to do, on your behalf.

Everything but `history` and `reviewed` is written once. `history` merges as
a union of steps, and `reviewed` only ever turns on.

fields.name: intent_hash
fields.doc:
Hex `H(method ‖ args)` from the warrant. The arguments themselves never
leave the agent: this is enough to match the feed row to the delta.

fields.name: executor
fields.doc: The relay account that executed the warrant, as the agent was told.

fields.name: chain
fields.doc: The chain this belongs to: the id of the row that started it.

fields.name: breach
fields.doc:
Why the rules say this needed you, when the agent acted anyway. Empty
when it did not.

ActionDef.doc: One action, as your agent proposes it and settings shows it.

fields.name: id
fields.doc: Stable within the app, e.g. `edit`; your setting for it is kept by it.

fields.name: label
fields.doc: What it is, for you: "Edit documents".

fields.name: description
fields.doc: One line on what it covers: "Write, format and reorder text".

fields.name: category
fields.doc:
The guard that always covers it, or empty when that depends on the
call (sending to someone new): then the category the agent names stands.

fields.name: writes
fields.doc: Whether it changes anything. An action that only reads always may run.

fields.name: methods
fields.doc: The app's methods it covers, by name.

ActionInput.doc: What the agent reports for one action.

fields.name: app
fields.doc: Short app key, e.g. `chat`, `sign`, `crm`. Policies are keyed by it.

fields.name: category
fields.doc: One of the guard categories, or empty for none.

fields.name: outcome
fields.doc: `proposed`, `done` or `failed`.

fields.name: note
fields.doc: What went wrong, for a `failed` outcome.

fields.name: chain
fields.doc:
The chain this continues: the id of the row that led to it (a
notification, or an earlier action). Empty starts a chain of its own.

fields.name: ask
fields.doc:
For a proposal: how you resolve it, beyond approve or decline. A
`choose` lets you approve with one of the options; a `reply` lets you
edit the agent's draft before it goes.

fields.name: grant
fields.doc:
For an outcome: the id of a proposal in the same app you approved with
"Allow for this session" (see [`SESSION_GRANT`]) in the last 12 hours.
Under the app's Ask mode, it is recorded without a breach. Older agents
omit it.

fields.name: subject
fields.doc:
What it touched in the app, as [`subject_key`] makes it (`""` for
nothing in particular). A notification about the same thing, with no
chain of its own, joins this action's chain. Older agents omit it.

ActionModeView.doc: One action you set apart from its app's mode.

ActionRule.doc:
Your setting for one action, kept by `<app>/<action id>`. It outlives the
set it was made under: a new version's action with the same id keeps it.

fields.name: mode
fields.doc: One of [`ACTION_MODES`], or empty to follow the app again.

ActionSet.doc: An app version's actions, as your agent learned them from its ABI.

fields.name: summary
fields.doc: One line for you: what changed, or what the set covers.

fields.name: status
fields.doc: [`LENS_PROPOSED`], [`LENS_APPROVED`] or [`LENS_REJECTED`].

AgentRule.doc:
A standing rule for one agent only ("Reply in one paragraph" for your
phone's agent): it goes into that agent's turns after your general rules,
which every agent keeps. Only you add or remove one; removing keeps the
row with `removed`, like [`Rule`].

fields.name: agent
fields.doc: The agent's name, as it reports in: "mero-bot@studio".

AgentRuleView.doc: One of your rules for one agent, as settings shows it.

AgentState.doc: The agent's global switch, stored under the single key `"main"`.

AgentView.doc: An agent and when it last said it was running (ms).

Answers.doc:
The question of your agent's that one of your messages answers, when you
answered it from its buttons. Kept beside your message by its id.

Archived.doc:
A chain you put away. It stays out of the feed until something new
happens in it, or until `until` passes ("later"); `until` 0 has no return
time. Unarchiving keeps the row with `archived: false`, so the latest
decision wins on every device.

fields.name: at
fields.doc: The chain's latest activity when it was put away: anything newer brings it back.

Ask.doc: How a row is best resolved in place. See [`ASK_KINDS`].

fields.name: kind
fields.doc: `""`, `confirm`, `reply` or `choose`.

fields.name: prompt
fields.doc: What the control says: "Reply in #launch", "Pick a slot", "Join the call".

fields.name: options
fields.doc: `choose`: the options (2 to 8). `reply`: suggested quick replies (up to 8).

fields.name: draft
fields.doc: `reply`: a draft to start from, e.g. the agent's proposed text.

Asked.doc:
What your agent asked you in a message, kept beside it by the message's
id, so messages written before agents could ask keep their layout.

Assignment.doc:
Which of your agents works in one app: the agent's name, as it reports in
(`mero-bot@<host>`). Only that agent takes the app's work (its new items,
your decisions about its actions, your messages about it) and only it may
call the app. An app with none is your default agent's: the private one.

fields.name: agent
fields.doc: Empty: back to the default agent.

AssignmentView.doc: Which agent works in one app, as settings shows it.

Attachment.doc:
An image on a message: a blob on your node, announced to the feed's
context, and what the client needs to show it before fetching it.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: The file's name as you picked it; may be empty for a pasted image.

fields.name: mime
fields.doc: One of [`IMAGE_TYPES`].

fields.name: size
fields.doc: Bytes, at most 10 MiB.

Attachments.doc:
A message's attachments. Kept beside the message, keyed by its id, so
messages written before attachments existed keep their layout.

Checkpoint.doc:
The latest checkpoint on one chain, kept by chain id. A new one replaces
it whole: last writer wins.

CheckpointInput.doc:
What the agent writes: [`crate::Hyperfeed::set_checkpoint`]'s `input`.
`done` and `next` are prose; the lists may be empty.

fields.name: done
fields.doc: What is done so far.

fields.name: next
fields.doc: The next step, as the session that picks it up should take it.

fields.name: branches
fields.doc: Git branches the task works on.

fields.name: worktrees
fields.doc: Worktrees (absolute paths) the task works in.

fields.name: prs
fields.doc: Pull requests: links, or `repo#number`.

fields.name: questions
fields.doc: What is still open: questions for the user, or doubts to settle.

fields.name: author
fields.doc: Who writes it: "mero-bot@studio".

CheckpointView.doc: A chain's latest checkpoint, as [`crate::Hyperfeed::checkpoint`] returns it.

fields.name: updated_at
fields.doc: When it was written (ms).

fields.name: archived
fields.doc: Chains put away right now (shown only by the `archived` filter).

FeedItem.doc:
One row of the feed. Actions and notifications share it so a client renders
one list; a field that does not apply to the row's kind is empty.

fields.name: chain
fields.doc:
The chain it belongs to, how many rows the chain has, and when anything
in it last happened (what the feed is ordered and paged by).

fields.name: status
fields.doc:
The current status and its note: an action's (`pending` … `done`) or a
notification's (`received`, `answered`, `delivered`, `failed`).

fields.name: history
fields.doc: Every step, oldest first.

fields.name: reviewed_at
fields.doc: When you kept an action the agent took without asking; 0 if not.

fields.name: from
fields.doc: Who sent a notification; for a message, [`FROM_YOU`] or [`FROM_AGENT`].

fields.name: reply_to
fields.doc: The message of yours an agent message answers.

fields.name: item_type
fields.doc: One of [`ITEM_TYPES`]; `""` for an untyped row.

fields.name: fields
fields.doc: The type's fields, a JSON object, or `""`.

fields.name: reply_call
fields.doc: The call that answers it in its app, or `""`; see [`Typed`].

fields.name: doing
fields.doc: Its latest step while the message is `thinking` ("Editing ChatView.tsx"), or `""`.

fields.name: doing_at
fields.doc: When that step started; 0 with no step.

fields.name: attachments
fields.doc: Images on a message of yours; empty for every other row.

fields.name: steps
fields.doc: What your agent did for it, step by step; empty for every other row.

fields.name: draft
fields.doc: The answer your agent has written so far, while the message is `thinking`; `""` otherwise.

fields.name: stop_at
fields.doc: When you asked your agent to stop working on it; 0 if you did not.

fields.name: headline
mode
fields.doc:
On a message of yours sent with a mode: `private` or `public` (see
[`MESSAGE_MODES`]). `""` when it was sent without one, and for every
other row; your agent's runtime then decides, usually by the chain's
last message that had one.

fields.name: superseded_by
fields.doc:
On a question (your agent's, or a notification's) that a newer one in
its chain replaced before you answered it: the newer one's id. Its
buttons are gone. `""` otherwise.

fields.name: answers
fields.doc:
On a message of yours sent from a question's buttons: that question's
id. `""` otherwise.

fields.name: answers_superseded
fields.doc:
Whether the question it answers had been replaced by a newer one: your
agent confirms against where things stand now before acting on it.

fields.name: held_by
fields.doc:
On a message: the agent whose session holds its chain right now
("mero-bot@studio"), or `""` when nobody does.

fields.name: held_since
fields.doc: Since when that session has held the chain; 0 when nobody does.

fields.name: subject
fields.doc:
On an action, what it touched; on a notification, what its reply goes
to; see [`subject_key`]. `""` for nothing in particular.

fields.name: counts
fields.doc:
Counts over the whole feed (muted apps excluded), not just this page,
so the filter tabs stay right while paging.

fields.name: next_before
fields.doc: Pass as `before` for the next page; 0 when there is none.

Folder.doc:
A folder an agent may use on its computer: an absolute path, or one under
`~`, and whether it may write there too.

Headline.doc:
A message's headline: one line for the feed row, its text behind "more".
Kept beside the message, keyed by its id, so messages written before
headlines keep their layout.

fields.name: owner
fields.doc: The account that created the feed; the only one that writes to it.

fields.name: typed
fields.doc: What a lens made of a notification, by the notification's id.

fields.name: lenses
fields.doc: How each app version's events become feed items, by `<app>@<application id>`.

fields.name: action_sets
fields.doc:
What your agent can do in each app version, by `<app>@<application id>`.
See [`actions`].

fields.name: action_rules
fields.doc: Your setting for each action apart from its app, by `<app>/<action id>`.

fields.name: archived
fields.doc: Chains you put away, by chain id.

fields.name: presence
fields.doc: Agents that report in, by name.

fields.name: asks
fields.doc: What your agent asked you, by its message's id.

fields.name: progress
fields.doc: Your agent's latest step on each message it is working on, by message id.

fields.name: attachments
fields.doc: Images on your messages, by the message's id.

fields.name: work
fields.doc: Your agent's turn on each of your messages it worked on, by message id.

fields.name: stops
fields.doc: Your requests to stop a turn, by message id.

fields.name: headlines
fields.doc: Headlines of messages written with one, by the message's id.

fields.name: modes
fields.doc: Which agent each of your messages sent with a mode is for, by the message's id.

fields.name: access
fields.doc: What you let each agent reach on its computer, by agent name.

fields.name: reach
fields.doc: What each agent last reported it can reach, by agent name.

fields.name: superseded
fields.doc: Questions a newer one in their chain replaced, by the question's id.

fields.name: answers
fields.doc:
The question each of your messages sent from its buttons answers, by
your message's id.

fields.name: leases
fields.doc: Which agent session works on each chain, by chain id.

fields.name: watches
fields.doc: "When X, do Y", polled by your agent's runtime, by id. See [`watches`].

fields.name: rules
fields.doc: Your standing rules, by id.

fields.name: rule_proposals
fields.doc: Rules your agent suggested, by id.

fields.name: checkpoints
fields.doc: Where each task stands, as your agent last wrote it, by chain id.

fields.name: prs
fields.doc:
The PRs your tasks link to, as your agent's runtime last saw them on
GitHub, by `owner/name#number`. See [`prs`].

fields.name: action_subjects
fields.doc: What each action touched, by the action's id.

fields.name: subject_chains
fields.doc: The chain that last touched each subject, by its key.

fields.name: links
fields.doc: Each task's links, by `<chain>|<subject>`. See [`links`].

fields.name: push_devices
fields.doc: Devices to push to, by endpoint. See [`push`].

fields.name: push_keys
fields.doc: The runtime's VAPID public key, under `vapid`.

fields.name: assignments
fields.doc: Which agent works in each app, by app key. See [`Assignment`].

fields.name: agent_rules
fields.doc: Your rules for one agent only, by id. See [`AgentRule`].

Lease.doc:
Which agent session is working on a chain, until when. A session claims a
chain before it starts a turn there, renews the lease while it works, and
releases it at the end; another session is refused the chain until then,
or until the lease runs out (the session died). Kept by chain id.

fields.name: session
fields.doc: The session's own id: unique per running agent process.

fields.name: agent
fields.doc: Who it is, in words: "mero-bot@studio".

fields.name: claimed_at
fields.doc: When this session took the chain; kept while it renews.

fields.name: expires_at
fields.doc: When the lease runs out; 0 once released.

LeaseView.doc: A session's lease on a chain, as [`Hyperfeed::claim_chain`] returns it.

fields.name: expires_at
fields.doc: 0 once released.

Lens.doc:
How one app version's events become feed items, as your agent learned it
from the app's ABI. Nothing uses a lens until you approve it.

fields.name: application_id
fields.doc: The app version it was learned from: a new version is learned again.

fields.name: spec
fields.doc: The lens itself, JSON (see the app's `lens` module).

fields.name: summary
fields.doc: One line for you: what it records and how it answers.

fields.name: status
fields.doc: [`LENS_PROPOSED`], [`LENS_APPROVED`] or [`LENS_REJECTED`].

Link.doc:
One link of a task, kept by `<chain>|<subject>`. Taking it off keeps the
row with `removed: true`, so your agent touching the thing again does not
bring it back; only you adding it does.

fields.name: subject
fields.doc: `<app>:<context>[:<id>]`, as [`crate::subject_key`] makes it.

fields.name: label
fields.doc:
What the chip says ("Agent digest card"); `""` keeps the one it has,
and a client names an unlabelled one from what it knows.

fields.name: by
fields.doc: `agent` or `you`.

fields.name: app
fields.doc:
The subject's parts: the app's key, its context, and the one thing in
it (`""` for the whole context: a chat, a board).

fields.name: activity
fields.doc: Notifications in the task about it: what teammates did there.

fields.name: last_at
fields.doc: The latest of them (ms); 0 with none.

Message.doc:
One message in a conversation with your agent, inside a chain.

You talk to your agent about a row by posting into its chain; a question
asked from nowhere starts a chain of its own. The agent's answers, and
anything it proposes or does because of them, land in the same chain.

fields.name: from
fields.doc: [`FROM_YOU`] or [`FROM_AGENT`].

fields.name: reply_to
fields.doc:
The message of yours this answers; empty for yours, and for an agent
message nobody asked for.

MessageMode.doc:
How private a message of yours is: one of [`MESSAGE_MODES`].
Kept beside the message, keyed by its id, so messages written before
modes keep their layout.

Notification.doc: One notification an app sent you, as your client saw it.

fields.name: id
fields.doc: The dedupe key the client derived from the source event.

fields.name: history
fields.doc:
`received`, then `answered` (your answer as the note), then
`delivered` or `failed` (the agent's note).

NotificationInput.doc: What your client saw for one notification.

fields.name: key
fields.doc:
Stable for the same event on every device, e.g.
`<context>:<root hash>:<index>`.

fields.name: chain
fields.doc: Empty starts a chain of its own, which is usual for a notification.

fields.name: ask
fields.doc: How to answer it from the feed, if it can be.

fields.name: item_type
fields.doc: What a lens made of it: one of [`ITEM_TYPES`]. Older clients omit these.

fields.name: fields
fields.doc: The type's fields, a JSON object.

fields.name: reply_call
fields.doc: The call that answers it in its app, a JSON object; see [`Typed`].

PrInput.doc: What [`crate::Hyperfeed::record_pr`] takes: the PR as GitHub shows it now.

fields.name: chain
fields.doc: The chain (task) that links to it; `""` keeps the one already recorded.

fields.name: repo
fields.doc: `owner/name`.

fields.name: state
fields.doc: `open`, `merged` or `closed`.

fields.name: base
fields.doc: The branch it merges into.

fields.name: default_branch
fields.doc: The repository's default branch.

fields.name: conflicts
fields.doc: GitHub found conflicts with the base.

fields.name: head_sha
fields.doc: The head commit the checks are on.

fields.name: checks
fields.doc: `green` (every check passed), `red` (one failed) or `pending`.

fields.name: failing
fields.doc: The failing checks' names, at most [`MAX_FAILING`].

fields.name: stacked_on
fields.doc: When `base` is another PR's branch, that PR's number; 0 otherwise.

fields.name: stacked_merged
fields.doc: Whether the PR it is stacked on is merged (its branch is dead).

PrSeen.doc: One PR as the runtime last saw it, kept by `owner/name#number`.

fields.name: seen_at
fields.doc: When the runtime looked (ms).

Presence.doc: When an agent last said it was running, by its name.

Progress.doc:
What your agent is doing right now for one of your messages: its latest
step, replaced by the next one. Kept beside the message by id, never in its
history, so a long turn adds no rows.

PushDevice.doc:
One device, kept by its endpoint. Taking it off keeps the row with
`removed: true`, so a device that synced late does not bring it back.

fields.name: quiet
fields.doc: Say only "Something needs you": no title, no text leaves your node.

fields.name: key
fields.doc: The VAPID public key it subscribed with.

PushDeviceInput.doc:
What [`crate::Hyperfeed::add_push_device`] takes: the browser's
`PushSubscription.toJSON()`, a name, and how much it may say.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: "Sandi's iPhone"; `""` is named "A device".

fields.name: key
fields.doc: The key it subscribed with: refused unless it is the current one.

fields.name: by
fields.doc: The runtime that holds its private half, by name.

PushKeyView.doc: The key as [`crate::Hyperfeed::push_key`] returns it; empty before a runtime set one.

Reach.doc: What one agent reported it can reach, latest report wins.

ReachLine.doc:
One agent profile an agent runs, as it reports it: which mode or route
it serves, its model, whether its model is attested, and what it can reach
besides your Calimero apps.

fields.name: serves
fields.doc: What it runs: `default`, or the kind of work a profile is routed to.

ReachView.doc: What one agent reported it can reach, as settings shows it.

Rule.doc:
One of your standing rules: a short line your agent keeps to on every
turn ("Never push to main", "Answer in English"). Only you add or remove
one; removing keeps the row with `removed`, so the latest decision wins on
every device.

RuleProposal.doc:
A rule your agent suggested after you corrected it. It changes nothing
until you approve it, which adds it as your own rule.

fields.name: why
fields.doc: Why your agent suggests it: the correction that led to it.

fields.name: chain
fields.doc: The chain where you corrected it, or `""`.

fields.name: status
fields.doc: [`RULE_PROPOSED`], [`RULE_APPROVED`] or [`RULE_DISMISSED`].

RuleProposalView.doc: A rule your agent suggested, as settings shows it.

RuleView.doc: One of your standing rules, as settings shows it.

fields.name: agents
fields.doc: Every agent that has reported in, most recent first.

fields.name: rules
fields.doc: Your standing rules, oldest first: your agent keeps to each on every turn.

fields.name: rule_proposals
fields.doc: Rules your agent suggested that wait for you, newest first.

fields.name: message_modes
fields.doc:
The modes a client offers beside Send. Always empty: which agent takes
your work is set per app (`assignments`). A `mode` argument is still
taken and kept, for clients made before assignments.

fields.name: access
fields.doc:
What you let each agent reach on its computer, by agent name. An agent
with no entry keeps its runtime's default.

fields.name: reach
fields.doc: What each agent last reported it can reach, by agent name.

fields.name: assignments
fields.doc:
Which agent works in each app you assigned, by app. An app with none
is your default agent's. Absent on a feed made before assignments.

fields.name: agent_rules
fields.doc:
Your rules for one agent only, by agent then oldest first. Each agent
keeps `rules` and then its own. Absent on a feed made before them.

fields.name: action_modes
fields.doc:
Actions you set apart from their app's mode, by app then action.
Absent on a feed made before actions.

Step.doc: One step in a row's history: a status, who said what about it, and when.

fields.name: note
fields.doc:
The note that came with it: the agent's ("NDA signed"), or your answer
(the reply you sent, the option you picked).

StopRequest.doc: You asked your agent to stop working on one of your messages.

Subject.doc:
What a row is about in another app, as a key: `<app>:<context>`, plus
`:<id>` for one thing in it (an issue, a doc, a thread). Kept two ways: by
the action's id (what it touched), and by the key (the chain that touched
it last), so a notification about the same thing joins that chain. See
[`subject_key`].

Superseded.doc:
A question that a newer one in its chain replaced: your agent asked
again, or an app sent a new question, before you answered this one. Kept
beside the row by its id. Its buttons go; an answer that still reaches it
goes to your agent marked as answering an old question.

fields.name: by
fields.doc: The newer question's id.

TurnStep.doc:
One step of your agent's turn on a message of yours: a tool it ran, a file
it edited, a write it made. Shown in the message's work block, never as a
row of its own.

fields.name: id
fields.doc: The agent's own id for the step, unique within the turn.

fields.name: title
fields.doc: What it is doing, in words: "Editing ChatView.tsx", "Running the tests".

fields.name: status
fields.doc: `running`, `waiting` (on your approval), `done` or `failed`.

fields.name: at
fields.doc: When the step started.

Typed.doc:
What a lens made of a notification: its type, the fields its card shows,
and the call that answers it in its app. Kept beside the notification, keyed
by its id, so rows recorded before lenses existed keep their layout.

fields.name: item_type
fields.doc: One of [`ITEM_TYPES`].

fields.name: fields
fields.doc: A JSON object: the fields of that type (`from`, `text`, `options`, …).

fields.name: reply_call
fields.doc:
A JSON object `{ "method", "args" }`: what your client calls in the
source context to answer, with `"=$answer"` where your answer goes.
Empty: answered by your agent, or not answerable from the feed.

Verdict.doc: The rules' answer for one prospective action.

fields.name: decision
fields.doc: `act`, `ask` or `refuse`.

fields.name: agent
fields.doc: Who set it: "mero-bot@studio", or "" for you.

fields.name: status
fields.doc:
[`WATCH_WATCHING`], [`WATCH_FIRING`], [`WATCH_DONE`], [`WATCH_FAILED`]
or [`WATCH_CANCELLED`].

fields.name: note
fields.doc: How the action went, or why it was cancelled.

fields.name: seen
fields.doc: What the runtime last saw, as one line: "3 of 5 checks passed, 2 running".

fields.name: fired_by
fields.doc: The session that fired it, and when.

WatchInput.doc:
What [`crate::Hyperfeed::add_watch`] takes. Every field is required; use
`""` or `0` where it does not apply.

fields.name: chain
fields.doc: The chain it reports to: the task it belongs to.

fields.name: condition
fields.doc: One of [`WATCH_CONDITIONS`].

fields.name: repo
fields.doc: The GitHub repository, `owner/name`.

fields.name: pr
fields.doc: The pull request's number, for a `pr_*` condition; 0 otherwise.

fields.name: branch
fields.doc:
The branch, for a `branch_*` condition; `""` is the repository's
default branch. `""` for a `pr_*` condition.

fields.name: action
fields.doc: One of [`WATCH_ACTIONS`]. `merge` goes with `pr_green` only.

fields.name: text
fields.doc:
The prompt for a `turn`, or what a `notify` tells you; may be `""` for
a `merge`.

fields.name: agent
fields.doc: Who sets it: "mero-bot@studio"; `""` for you.

WatchView.doc: A watch, as the feed returns it.

Work.doc:
Your agent's turn on one of your messages, as it goes: its steps, and the
answer it has written so far. Kept beside the message by id and replaced
whole by each report, so a long turn adds no rows.

fields.name: draft
fields.doc: The answer so far, while the agent writes it; `""` before it starts.

methods.name: action_sets
methods.doc:
Every app's actions, newest first: what your agent learned for each
app version, and whether you approved it. An app's newest approved set
is the one in force.

methods.name: add_agent_rule
methods.doc:
Add a rule for one agent only: it keeps it after your general rules,
which every agent keeps. Only you add rules; the same rule twice for
the same agent is kept once.

methods.name: add_link
methods.doc:
Link a thing in another app to the task in `chain`: `subject` as
[`subject_key`] makes it, a `label` for its chip, `by` you or your
agent. What teammates do there joins the task from now on. Adding one
again relabels it; you adding one you took off brings it back.

methods.name: add_push_device
methods.doc:
A phone (or any browser) to push to: its push subscription, a name,
and `quiet` to say only "Something needs you". Owner only; adding one
again updates it. At most [`MAX_PUSH_DEVICES`]; the oldest makes room.

methods.name: add_rule
methods.doc:
Add a standing rule: one short line your agent keeps to on every turn.
Only you add rules; the same rule twice is kept once.

methods.name: add_watch
methods.doc:
Set a watch: when its condition is met (a PR's checks green or red, a
PR merged, a branch's CI green or red), its action runs once (merge
the PR, start an agent turn with `text`, or tell you), reported in its
chain. Your agent's runtime polls it; the same watch twice is kept once.

methods.name: agent_ack
methods.doc:
The agent takes up one of your messages (`thinking`), or gives up on it
(`failed`, with why). Taking it up is how you know an agent is there.

methods.name: agent_ask
methods.doc:
[`Self::agent_say`] that leaves something to you: a question to
`reply` to, or options to `choose` from. The message needs you, in To
do, until you say something in its chain; your words are its answer.
Use it whenever the work is not finished without you, so a chain is
only done when it is.

Takes a `headline` as [`Self::agent_say`] does.

methods.name: agent_progress
methods.doc:
Your agent says what it is doing on one of your messages it has taken
up (`thinking`): "Running the tests", "Editing ChatView.tsx". Each call
replaces the last, so you see its latest step and nothing piles up.

methods.name: agent_reach
methods.doc:
An agent saying what it can reach: one line per agent profile it runs.
Shown to you in Controls beside what you set with `set_access`.

methods.name: agent_say
methods.doc:
The agent says something in a chain: an answer to one of your
messages (`reply_to`, which marks it answered), or, with `reply_to`
empty, a note of its own in a chain that exists.

A long answer takes a `headline`: one line of at most 80 characters,
which the feed row shows, with `text` (up to 32 KB) behind "more" and
in full in the chat. Without one, `text` keeps to 2000 bytes. Older
agents omit it.

methods.name: agent_seen
methods.doc:
An agent saying it is running. The feed shows it as live while it
keeps reporting; mero-bot calls this every half minute.

methods.name: agent_work
methods.doc:
Your agent reports its turn on one of your messages: every step so far
(each with its own `id`, a `title` in words, a `status` of `running`,
`waiting`, `done` or `failed`, and when it started) and the answer it
has written so far as `draft`. Each call replaces the last, so the
turn never adds rows: send it whenever a step starts or ends, and
every few seconds while the answer is being written. The steps stay
on the message after the turn; the draft shows only while it is
`thinking`.

methods.name: answer_ask
methods.doc:
Answer one question your agent asked, from its buttons: `text` is the
option you picked, or your reply. It is your next message in the
question's chain, and goes to your agent like any other.

A question a newer one replaced can still be answered (a screen that
had not caught up yet, another device): it is marked answered, the
newer question stays open, and your message carries
`answers_superseded`, so your agent confirms against where things
stand now before acting on it.

methods.name: answer_notification
methods.doc:
Answer a notification from the feed: the reply to send, the option you
picked, or `""` to confirm. Your agent carries it out in the source app
and reports with [`Hyperfeed::complete_answer`]. A failed delivery can be
answered again.

methods.name: approve_rule
methods.doc:
Approve a rule your agent suggested: it becomes one of your rules,
added by you.

methods.name: archive
methods.doc:
Pause the agent: every write it wants to make becomes a proposal.
Put chains away: each leaves the feed until something new happens in
it, or until `until` (ms; 0 = no return time) for "later". Returns how
many were put away.

methods.name: cancel_watch
methods.doc:
Cancel a watch still watching, with an optional note why. A watch that
already fired cannot be called back.

methods.name: chain
methods.doc: Every row in a chain, oldest first: the whole flow, muted apps included.

methods.name: chain_lease
methods.doc: Who holds `chain` right now: a lease that has not run out, or none.

methods.name: check_action
methods.doc:
What your rules say about an action before the agent takes it. Name
the app `method` it calls: once you approved the app's actions, they
decide what the call is, not `category` and `writes`. Older agents omit
it and are judged by what they say.

methods.name: checkpoint
methods.doc: The latest checkpoint on `chain`, or none: read it before acting there.

methods.name: claim_chain
methods.doc:
An agent session takes `chain` for `ttl_ms` before it starts a turn
there: one turn per chain at a time, across machines. Refused while
another session holds an unexpired lease; a lease that ran out (its
session died) can be taken. Claiming a chain the session already
holds renews it. `agent` names it for the chat ("mero-bot@studio");
older agents omit it.

methods.name: complete_action
methods.doc:
The agent reports what happened after you approved, asked for a retry,
or asked for an undo.

methods.name: complete_answer
methods.doc:
The agent reports whether it carried out your answer to a notification:
sent the reply, cast the vote, accepted the invite.

methods.name: decide_actions
methods.doc:
Approve or turn down the actions your agent proposed for an app
version. Once approved they decide what each call in the app is, and
a method none of them names asks you every time.

methods.name: decide_lens
methods.doc:
Approve or turn down a lens your agent proposed. Only an approved lens
turns an app's events into feed items, and only for the app version it
was learned from.

methods.name: dismiss_rule
methods.doc: Turn down a rule your agent suggested.

methods.name: feed
methods.doc:
The feed: one row per chain, newest activity first.

A row is the chain's **lead**: the latest step that needs you if any
does, otherwise the latest still underway (an action approved, retrying
or being undone; your message waiting or being answered; your answer
being delivered), otherwise the latest row. So a chain is settled only
when everything in it is. Its `chain_len` says how many rows the chain
holds and `needs_you` whether any of them needs you; read them all with
[`Hyperfeed::chain`].

`filter` keeps chains holding an action (`agent`), a notification
(`notifications`), or something that needs you (`needs_you`); `app_key`
keeps chains that touch that app; `before` pages by `chain_at` (0 = from
the newest). The counts are over chains, for the whole feed.

methods.name: finish_watch
methods.doc: How the fired action went: `done` or `failed`, with a note.

methods.name: fire_watch
methods.doc:
The runtime takes a watch whose condition it saw met, before it acts:
`watching → firing`, refused for any other status. Of every session
polling, exactly one gets it, once.

methods.name: init
methods.doc:
No arguments: the frontend's context-creation flow sends `{}`. The
creator owns the feed.

methods.name: item
methods.doc: One row, by id, whichever kind it is.

methods.name: lenses
methods.doc:
Every lens, newest first: what your agent learned for each app version,
and whether you approved it.

methods.name: links
methods.doc:
The links of the task in `chain`, oldest first, each with how much
teammates did there (its notifications in the task).

methods.name: mark_all_seen
methods.doc: Mark every notification seen.

methods.name: mark_seen
methods.doc:
Mark notifications seen. Unknown ids are skipped; returns how many
changed.

methods.name: open_questions
methods.doc:
Your messages your agent has not answered yet, oldest first: what an
agent that was away picks up when it starts.

methods.name: propose_actions
methods.doc:
The agent proposes an app version's actions, learned from its ABI:
which methods make up each thing you would recognise ("Edit
documents"), whether it writes, and the guard that covers it. It waits
for you; the app's newest approved set stays in force meanwhile. The
same actions proposed again change nothing.

methods.name: propose_lens
methods.doc:
The agent proposes a lens for one app version, learned from its ABI.
It waits for you: an approved lens is replaced only by a new proposal,
which waits again. The same spec proposed again changes nothing.

methods.name: propose_rule
methods.doc:
Your agent suggests a standing rule after you corrected it: `text` is
the rule, `why` the correction, `chain` where it happened. It waits
for you in Controls and in the chat; nothing changes until you approve
it. A rule you already have, or one already waiting, is not suggested
twice.

methods.name: prs
methods.doc:
The PRs the runtime recorded for `chain` (`""`: every chain), the most
recently seen first.

methods.name: push_devices
methods.doc: The devices to push to, newest first.

methods.name: push_key
methods.doc: The key phones subscribe with; empty before a runtime set one.

methods.name: record_action
methods.doc:
Record an action: a proposal for you to approve, or an outcome.

A proposal the rules refuse is an error. An outcome the rules say
needed you is recorded with a breach, never dropped, unless the app's
mode alone asked for you and its `grant` is a session you allowed.

methods.name: record_notification
methods.doc:
Record a notification your client saw.

Every device records what it sees, and the same event arrives under the
same key on each, so a key already recorded within
[`DEDUPE_WINDOW_MS`] returns that row and records nothing. The same key
later is a new event — the source context came back to a state it had
been in — and is stored as `<key>#1`, `<key>#2`, … Two devices reporting
that occurrence derive the same id, so their rows still merge.

methods.name: record_pr
methods.doc:
Your agent's runtime records a PR a task links to as GitHub shows it
now: state, base and default branch, conflicts, head commit, checks
(the failing ones named) and the PR it is stacked on. Owner only; one
row per PR, the oldest of [`MAX_PRS`] dropped to make room.

methods.name: release_chain
methods.doc:
The session lets `chain` go at the end of its turn. Returns whether it
held it: letting go of a chain it does not hold changes nothing.

methods.name: remove_agent_rule
methods.doc: Remove one of your rules for one agent.

methods.name: remove_link
methods.doc:
Take a link off the task in `chain`. Nothing new about it joins the
task, and your agent touching it again does not bring it back.

methods.name: remove_push_device
methods.doc:
Stop pushing to a device: you took it off, or its push service said
it is gone.

methods.name: remove_rule
methods.doc: Remove one of your standing rules.

methods.name: renew_chain
methods.doc:
The session holding `chain` keeps it for another `ttl_ms` while it
works. Refused once another session has it, or when this one never
did or released it: it should stop, not carry on beside the other.

methods.name: resolve_action
methods.doc:
Approve or decline a proposal, retry or drop a failure, ask for an
undo, or keep an action the agent took without asking.

`answer` goes with an approval when the proposal has an [`Ask`]: one of
its options for `choose`, the text to send for `reply` (the agent's
draft, edited or not). Every other decision takes `""`.

methods.name: say
methods.doc:
Talk to your agent: about a chain (`chain` = its id), or about
anything (`chain` empty, which starts a new chain). Your agent picks it
up, answers in the chain, and may propose or act there under your rules.

A long message takes a `headline`, as [`Self::agent_say`] does. Older
clients omit it.

`mode` says how private it is, and so which of your agents takes it:
`private` or `public` (see [`MESSAGE_MODES`]). Omitted or empty, it
has none, and your agent's runtime decides. Older clients omit it.

methods.name: say_with
methods.doc:
[`Self::say`] with images: up to four, each a blob you uploaded to your
node and announced to this context. With an image, `text` may be empty.

methods.name: set_access
methods.doc:
What `agent` (its name, as it reports in) may reach on its computer
besides your Calimero apps: `folders` (each with or without writes),
a `shell`, and the `web`. It replaces what was set before. Your
agent's runtime refuses this method to the agent, so only you widen
or narrow it.

methods.name: set_action_mode
methods.doc:
Set one action apart from its app's mode: `act` without asking, `ask`
first, `off`, or empty to follow the app again. Your guards and the
pause still apply.

methods.name: set_assignment
methods.doc:
Assign `app_key` to `agent` (its name, as it reports in): from then on
only that agent takes the app's work and calls it. An empty `agent`
gives the app back to your default agent. Your agent's runtime refuses
this method to the agent, so only you move an app between agents.

methods.name: set_checkpoint
methods.doc:
Your agent writes where the task in `chain` stands: what is done, the
next step, its branches, worktrees and PRs, and what is still open. It
replaces the chain's last checkpoint, so a new session can pick the
task up from it. The limits are in `checkpoint.rs`.

methods.name: set_push_key
methods.doc:
Your agent's runtime keeps its VAPID public key here, for phones to
subscribe with; `by` names the runtime that holds the private half.
Owner only. A different key drops every device: each subscribes again.

methods.name: settings
methods.doc:
Your rules: the pause switch, every app you set a policy for, every
guard (defaults included), your standing rules, and the rules your
agent suggested that wait for you.

methods.name: start_task
methods.doc:
Spin a task off the chat in `from`: `text` is your message that opens
it, in a chain of its own, with its own post, workspace, checkpoint
and PRs. The chat keeps a link to the task (`hyperfeed:task:<chain>`)
and the task one back (`hyperfeed:from:<chain>`). Takes a `headline`
as [`Self::say`] does, which names the task's link. Returns the
task's first message; its chain is the task.

methods.name: stop
methods.doc:
You ask your agent to stop working on one of your messages. One it has
not taken up yet is closed at once, "Stopped by you"; one it is working
on (`thinking`) keeps the request, and your agent ends its turn and
marks the message failed, "Stopped by you". Asking twice changes
nothing.

methods.name: touch_subject
methods.doc:
Your agent touched `subject` (see [`subject_key`]) for the task in
`chain` with a write that has no row of its own: a step of its turn on
a message of yours. A notification about it then joins `chain`, as
for an action that names it.

methods.name: unarchive
methods.doc: Bring chains back into the feed.

methods.name: watch_seen
methods.doc:
What the runtime last saw of a watching watch's condition, as one line
("3 of 5 checks passed, 2 running"). Only a change is written.

methods.name: watches
methods.doc:
The watches in `chain` (`""`: every chain), oldest first, whatever
their status.

events.name: ActionsChanged
events.doc:
An app's actions were proposed, approved or turned down: re-read
`action_sets`.

events.name: ArchiveChanged
events.doc: Chains were put away or brought back: re-read the feed.

events.name: ChainLeaseChanged
events.doc: An agent session took a chain, or let it go: re-read who is on it.

events.name: CheckpointChanged
events.doc: Your agent wrote where a task stands: re-read its `checkpoint`.

events.name: LensChanged
events.doc: A lens was proposed, approved or turned down: re-read `lenses`.

events.name: MessagePosted
events.doc: A message in a chain: yours (your agent should answer) or its answer.

events.name: PrChanged
events.doc:
Your agent's runtime saw a PR change on GitHub (`owner/name#number`):
re-read `prs`.

events.name: PushChanged
events.doc: A device to push to, or the push key, changed: re-read `push_devices`.

events.name: StopRequested
events.doc:
You asked your agent to stop working on message `id`: it ends the turn
and marks the message failed, "Stopped by you".

events.name: WatchChanged
events.doc: A watch was set, fired, finished or cancelled: re-read `watches`.
